title: Perovskite Photovoltaics in January-June 2026: Defect passivation, interface and contact engineering
abstract: Evaluation of 3328 publications across 6 months, with 884 examined in depth, reveals that reported efficiency records mask severe mechanistic contradictions and pervasive validation deficits across the discipline. Independent verification remained scarce: only 114 investigations reported an accredited power conversion efficiency (PCE), with the certified frontier reaching 34.85% in monolithic tandems and 27.6% in single-junction cells. Rather than advancing across the observation window, certified performance remained confined within a narrow efficiency corridor where contradictory physical models yielded indistinguishable macroscopic photovoltaic parameters. These certified benchmarks were attained through competing interfacial and bulk defect mitigation strategies. At top interfaces, reports diverged sharply on whether non-radiative recombination suppression requires reconstructing low-dimensional capping phases or whether such layers impose deleterious carrier extraction bottlenecks. At buried contacts, self-assembled monolayer (SAM) engineering alternated between static electrostatic dipole alignment using polar co-adsorbents and mitigating dynamic interfacial chemical redox reactions, while tandem subcell coupling contested whether current matching demands laterally conductive transparent conducting oxides or direct tin oxide recombination layers across textured interfaces. Concurrently, formamidinium lead triiodide phase stabilization conflicted between non-destructive contact-triggered templating without interdiffusion and active cation exchange driven by Ostwald ripening. Device scaling imposed an uncompromising area penalty, with the maximum certified aperture reaching \qty{655.2}{\centi\meter}$^2$ at an efficiency of 26.8%. This scaling loss stems from conflicting precursor-solvent coordination kinetics during blade and slot-die coating, where suppressing intermediate solvent adducts conflicts with Lewis-base coordination required to retard premature nucleation, compounded by drying non-uniformities, localized sheet resistance penalties, and pinhole multiplication. Operational durability evidence is severely deficient across the field: only 39 publications reported stability lifetimes to the defined retention threshold, with the longest reaching \qty{4100}{\hour}. Evidence for long-term operational resilience remains thin, as operando structural characterization demonstrates that bulky passivators designed to relieve lattice strain induce localized lattice expansion and mechanochemical fatigue under thermal stress, while buried SAM contacts degrade through unresolved competition between field-driven lateral aggregation into isolated clusters and out-of-plane molecular desorption. Reporting practices reinforce this empirical deficit: only 39 studies implemented standardized International Summit on Organic Photovoltaic Stability (ISOS) protocols. Abstract-level text extraction confirms that while 52.1% of publications stated an efficiency, only 8.5% reported independent certification, showing that most claims rely on uncertified dynamic sweeps without aperture masking verification, spectral mismatch calibration, or steady-state maximum power point tracking (MPPT). Mechanistic synthesis indicates that apparent efficiency advances frequently reflect transient electrostatic screening and interfacial dipole realignment rather than permanent electronic defect remediation. Because diametrically opposed physical models produce indistinguishable macroscopic parameters, standard current-voltage characterization cannot separate interfacial recombination velocity from bulk trap states. Resolving whether operational degradation proceeds through interfacial redox, lateral contact dewetting, or mobile point defect accumulation requires operando, spatially resolved transient spectroscopy paired with depth-resolved photoemission under simultaneous electrical bias, continuous illumination, and elevated temperature, alongside standardized ISOS aging on certified apertures.
